question.text: Consider the triangle $\triangle{ABC}$ shown above. The line segment $\overline{AH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overline{BC}.$ If $ m\angle{ACB} = 125^\circ,$ calculate $ m\angle{HAC}.$
question.explanation:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align} m\angle HCA + m\angle ACB & = 180^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle HCA + 125^\circ&= 180^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle HCA &= 55^\circ. \end{align}

Note that $\triangle AHC$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to $180^\circ,$ we have \begin{align} m\angle{HCA} + m\angle{HAC} + m\angle{AHC} & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] 55^\circ + m\angle{HAC} + 90^\circ & = 180^\circ\\[3pt] m\angle{HAC} + 145^\circ & = 180^\circ \\[3pt] m\angle{HAC} & = 35^\circ. \end{align}

question.text: Given $\triangle{PQR}$ shown above, which of the following diagrams represents the height corresponding to $\overline{PR}?$
question.explanation:
The height (or altitude) corresponding to $\overline{PR}$ is a line segment that

  • runs from the opposite vertex $Q$ to the line $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR},$ and

  • is perpendicular to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR}.$

To draw the height, we proceed as follows:

  • Extend the line segment $\overline{PR}.$
  • Draw the perpendicular from $Q$ to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PR}.$
